description: A workspace member creates a new person record by sending a GraphQL mutation to the main /graphql endpoint, and the workspace has a webhook subscribed to person-creation events. Trace the complete server-side path from the incoming HTTP request to the outbound HTTP POST that reaches the webhook URL. For each hop give the file and function, and say which hops cross an asynchronous boundary (in-process event emitter or message queue) and what the payload looks like on each side of the boundary.
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only
alternatives: The same mutation over REST or from a workflow/agent tool skips steps 1-6 but joins at WorkspaceRepository (steps 11+).
A request that opens an explicit transaction (nested relation create, record sharing) goes through WorkspaceDataSource.transaction so emission is deferred to after commit.
The path via the generated GraphQL schema (WorkspaceSchemaFactory) exists but is used for SDK client generation, not for serving /graphql.

source.verification: Third party reads each cited line and checks the call/enqueue/emit named in the edge column; steps 19/23 are verifiable by matching the job class name string passed to add() with the @Process argument in the next step. Run webhook-rate-limit.integration-spec.ts (needs DB+Redis) to observe delivery end to end.
source.notes: Confounders: (a) the question says 'GraphQL resolver' but /graphql workspace queries bypass the generated resolvers via DirectExecutionService (step 1-5); an agent that stops at WorkspaceResolverBuilderService will be wrong. (b) job names equal class names (Process(Class.name)), so grep for the string finds both enqueue and handler. (c) Line numbers are for snapshot bde4ff13. Not tool-verified by running.
